To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Global greening has offset ~12% of global warming over the past three decades.”

1) the net global cooling effect of greening is 0.41 Wm-2; 2) the net global greening effect is 0.12 Wm-2 of the 0.95 Wm-2 warming that has occurred over the 1982–2015 period; 3) this cooling effect has been offset by a warming effect of 0.29 Wm-2 from the increase in the global land-surface albedo; and

(i) the global greening of vegetation over land has been accompanied by a global cooling trend, which is (ii) caused by the combined effect of the cooling of land surfaces due to the increase in albedo (i.e. the fraction of solar radiation reflected by the land surface), and the warming of the lower atmosphere caused by an increase in the greenhouse effect (the greenhouse effect is caused by the absorption of infrared radiation by the atmosphere).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of vegetation in the Earth's climate system, and the impact of climate change and land-use change on vegetation.
the role of vegetation in the Earth system, including the role of vegetation as an agent of change and a target of change.

the following topics: the impact of climate change on the environment, the impact of climate variability on the environment, climate and the carbon cycle, the impact of land cover changes on climate, the impact of vegetation on climate, and the impact of climate on vegetation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the greening effect has been cooling the Earth by 12% over the past three decades and that the greening is not a net contributor to global warming.
the global climate system has been cooling over the past 3 decades, and that the global cooling has been caused by the increase of the leaf area index.
the net effect of greening has been cooling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the greening of the Earth has offset 12% of the global warming that would have occurred during the past 30 years.
the net effect of greening has been to reduce the magnitude of warming over land.
the greening of the land surface has been a cooling influence on the climate system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vegetation feedbacks to climate change have been underestimated.

the global climate system is more complex than we previously thought, and that we need to consider more than just the radiative effects of vegetation when assessing the impact of greening on regional climate.
the global climate system is more sensitive to changes in the land surface than previously recognized.
